speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Our pioneer leaders knew that keeping Singapore clean would enhance our people's health and improve our quality of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: So, we embarked on programmes to improve public hygiene, stamp out public littering and clean up our rivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Today, Singapore is widely regarded as one of the cleanest cities in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the importance of maintaining high public hygiene and sanitation standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Maintaining public hygiene was our first line of defence in protecting ourselves and our loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Even as pandemic risks subside, we must not rest on our laurels and forget the tough lessons learnt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Just as importantly, COVID-19 showed how critical our environmental services like cleaning and waste management are to the well-being of our nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Our cleaning and waste management businesses and their workers support day-to-day functions in our economy and safeguard our population's health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Our waste management sector also plays an important role in helping Singapore achieve our zero-waste ambition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We need to support our cleaning and waste management businesses and their workers and ensure they stand ready to meet future demands while managing manpower challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Even so, we cannot just rely on our cleaners and waste management workers to keep Singapore clean.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Keeping Singapore clean is a whole-of-society responsibility that everyone must contribute to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Bill will give effect to policies that strengthen our waste management and cleaning sectors and ensure that maintaining a clean and hygienic living environment continues to be our collective responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: First, we wish to uplift our resident workers in the waste management sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will benefit some 3,000 eligible resident employees, including crew and drivers of waste collection trucks, sorters and machine operators in waste collection and recycling facilities and supervisors performing certain roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The PWM will uplift wages and boost productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The TCWM, comprising unions, Government agencies and service buyers, has proposed a six-year schedule of wage increases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: There will also be minimum amounts and scheduled increases for overtime payments and annual bonuses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: A structured career ladder, stipulating higher job roles, higher wages and minimum training requirements, will enhance career progression and prepare the industry for higher-value work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Bill gives legislative effect to the recommendations of the TCWM and implements the PWM through the licensing regime for companies providing waste collection and materials recovery services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Sections 23 and 31 are amended to require applicants for waste disposal licences and waste collector licences, each called a waste management licence, to submit a Progressive Wage Plan with their licence application.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Progressive Wage Plan will cover details on the wage components paid to workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The new sections 23A and 31AA provide for the making of regulations to impose licence conditions relating to the training of workers and payment of progressive wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This clearly establishes the PWM within the ambit of the EPHA and the waste management licensing regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Sections 23A(2)(d) and 31AA(2)(d) enable the imposition of licence conditions to prohibit waste management licensees from deploying individuals for waste management work unless they are their employees or employees of other waste management licensees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will ensure that all waste management workers can benefit from the PWM wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The new section 31DA will require the Commissioner for Labour to specify by way of an order the wage-related components for each class of waste management workers under the PWM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will provide greater clarity and certainty to the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To effectively monitor compliance with licensing conditions, including those of the PWM, the new section 31DB empowers the Director-General of Public Health and any authorised officers to require licensees to produce relevant hardcopy or electronic records such as wage and training records of the licensees' workers for inspection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: I will next elaborate on changes we will introduce to the cleaning business licensing framework to build a resilient and productive cleaning sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We started on the journey to professionalise the cleaning sector as early as July 2010, when a Voluntary Accreditation Scheme was introduced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The pandemic has intensified the urgency for cleaning businesses to transform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With rising demands for quality cleaning services, coupled with growing manpower challenges, cleaning businesses need to deepen their competencies, adopt productivity solutions and create better employment opportunities to attract and retain workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To build capabilities and raise public health standards of cleaning businesses, the cleaning business licensing framework will be enhanced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Key elements of the voluntary Enhanced Clean Mark Accreditation Scheme will also be merged with the current cleaning business licensing scheme into a single framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Bill will amend sections 80F to 80I to implement the revised cleaning business licensing framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The new classes of licences will come with a two-year validity period but the application requirements such as training, paid-up capital, bizSAFE certification and compliance history with certain written laws for each class of licence will be different.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Class 3 licence, which is non-renewable, retains the same requirements as the current licensing scheme without imposing any new requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: New cleaning businesses can be granted a Class 3 licence but upon its expiry, must apply for a Class 2 or Class 1 licence to continue operating.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Class 2 licensees will need to meet the new paid-up capital and bizSAFE certification requirements that are applicable to that class of licensees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The bizSAFE certification ensures that cleaning businesses inculcate a culture of workplace safety for its workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Class 1 licence is for cleaning businesses that want to further differentiate themselves in terms of capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It provides greater assurance to service buyers that the licensees are equipped with more resources, experience and capabilities to undertake larger cleaning contracts and are committed to raising the skill level and competencies of their employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Existing cleaning businesses will be able to transit to the new framework easily with the Class 3 licence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: They would have sufficient time, at least two years, to grow their capabilities and transit to the higher classes of licence as the revised framework will come into effect on 1 January 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Prior to revising the licensing framework, the National Environment Agency (NEA) had consulted and received support from cleaning businesses on the revised framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA will continue to work closely with key stakeholders and partner agencies to ensure a smooth transition for the cleaning businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Bill amendments will also empower the making of regulations to impose a licence condition to prohibit cleaning business licensees from deploying individuals to carry out cleaning work unless those individuals are their employees or employed by other cleaning business licensees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will ensure that all cleaners benefit from the licensing framework and resident workers are paid PWM wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In addition, persons who supply cleaners will be required to be licensed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Such persons include companies which supply manpower to other cleaning businesses or premises owners to carry out cleaning work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The enhanced licensing framework will ensure that cleaning businesses continue to upskill their workforce and pay progressive wages, while encouraging investment in innovation and technology to improve productivity and service delivery to boost their competitiveness as well as overcome manpower constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Service buyers will benefit from better services and can also make more informed decisions in selecting cleaning businesses, based on the service buyers' needs and scope of cleaning work that they require.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Currently, Government Procuring Entities are required to engage only cleaning businesses with a Clean Mark Gold Accreditation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With the revised framework incorporating key elements of the Enhanced Clean Mark Accreditation Scheme, NEA will work with the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to require Government Procuring Entities to engage only cleaning businesses with a Class 1 Licence in the longer term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These are automated and enclosed systems that make waste collection more hygienic and efficient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Since April 2018, all new developments for strata-titled properties with 500 or more residential dwelling units are required to implement the PWCS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: As the number of PWCS implemented in strata-titled developments in Singapore is expected to rise, there is a need to ensure that the equipment can be operated effectively over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Currently, the existing legislation places responsibility on building owners to maintain their waste collection systems, such as refuse lifts, chutes and chute chambers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The PWCS, which consists of a network of pipes to convey waste by air suction to the refuse bin centre, is also an integral part of the waste collection system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Bill will repeal and re-enact section 11 to make it clear that building owners have the responsibility to maintain their PWCS that serve the buildings and empower the Director-General of Public Health to take enforcement actions against owners who do not maintain, repair and replace their PWCS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Second, on littering from residential flats which is a persistent, growing issue that blights our heartlands, affecting many of our estates islandwide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA has conducted extensive public education and outreach with stakeholders such as the Town Councils and Grassroots Organisations, enhanced its enforcement capabilities and increased public awareness on the environmental consequences of high-rise littering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Despite these interventions, such a rate of increase, if allowed to persist, will be detrimental to public health – our estates risk getting increasingly dirty and unsafe, and our resources will never be enough to clean up after the offenders or catch and enforce against them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Stronger action is needed to address the root of the issue and prevent high-rise littering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will do this by introducing presumptions to place greater onus on owners and tenants of residential flats to prevent littering acts from being committed from their units in the first place, and when such offences have been committed, for them to take greater responsibility to identify the offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Today, when feedback is received on high-rise littering from residential flats onto any public place, NEA will first work with relevant Town Councils to issue advisories to residents in the affected block to advise them not to commit high-rise littering from their flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: If the high-rise littering issue persists, NEA will deploy surveillance cameras to monitor the blocks and identify the unit from which the high-rise littering is committed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Video footage from surveillance cameras detailing the act of high-rise littering from a specific unit is then used for focused investigations leading to enforcement action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: However, the investigation process can be laborious and protracted, inhibiting effective enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Even if the residential units where the litter was thrown have been clearly identified from the evidence, significant effort is still needed to identify the offender before enforcement can follow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The existing provision in the EPHA1987 requires flat owners to provide information on the identity of every occupant of the flat at the time of the offence and NEA may have to interview every occupant to identify the offender.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Despite our best efforts, there are cases where NEA cannot identify the offender because all the occupants deny knowledge of the act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This means that even with evidence that littering has been committed from a flat, NEA is unable to take enforcement action in such cases, which undermines deterrence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For the relevant presumption clause to take effect, the evidence would need to clearly capture the act of littering and the flat from which the litter had originated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Images or footage captured by NEA's enforcement cameras would be our main source of evidence, but we will also accept such evidence if submitted by members of the public, subject to the quality of the evidence necessary to support our enforcement actions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Flat owners or tenants can rebut the presumption through various means in order not to be held responsible under the presumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Namely, a flat owner or tenant can produce evidence that he or she was not present in the flat at the time of the offence, prove that someone else had committed that offence or provide the identity of the person whom he or she reasonably believes to be the offender.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Flat owners or tenants will be given a reasonable stipulated time period to produce such information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This would allow for more effective enforcement and at the same time, spur flat owners and tenants to prevent their occupants from littering from their flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The current process of issuing advisories when feedback is first received and deploying surveillance cameras in persistent cases will not change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Even after the owner or tenant has shown that he or she was not present in the flat at the time of offence or provided the identity of the person whom the owner or tenant reasonably believes to have committed the littering, NEA will continue to investigate, including interviewing any relevant witnesses such as the other occupiers or the suspect named by the owner or tenant so as to verify the information provided.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA will ensure that our investigation process remains robust and that the law is applied judiciously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Care will be exercised in investigating cases committed by vulnerable groups such as young children and the elderly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For the elderly or other vulnerable individuals, NEA will engage the individuals and their family members or caregivers and work with social agencies to provide further assistance where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Third, we will enable more effective enforcement of the EPHA to ensure we maintain a clean and liveable environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Currently, Section 20 of the EPHA already prohibits the use of a vehicle to dump or dispose of waste in public places, which poses environmental and public health risks and is a blight on public places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is necessary because there have been instances of supervisors improperly instructing their workers to illegally dispose of waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This could have been due to protracted investigations for complex cases or the late referral of cases by members of the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We must continue to help and support our waste management and cleaning companies and workers to upgrade, transform and thrive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will enable them to deliver high-quality services with a better skilled and engaged workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We must also take a firm stance against actions that create disamenities and endanger public health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Keeping our living environment clean has been and will continue to remain a shared responsibility for all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a Bill that is a step in the right direction and one I wholeheartedly support.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It will address a lot of the high-rise littering issues we all see on the ground and very importantly, it will uplift our workers in the cleaning and waste disposal sector.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That said, I just have three points of clarification to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the Progressive Wage Model (PWM).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: PWM is also about improving productivity, which will improve business profits for employers and service buyers also enjoy better service standards and quality.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But all these cannot happen if the bulk of the workforce is not getting the PWM.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Both our local and migrant workforce deserve to earn fair and liveable wages.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I shared in this House previously about how I have seen first-hand the sacrifices that our migrant cleaners make to keep our homes clean.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2019, I visited Bangladesh and invited all our Nee Soon East cleaners' families to lunch in Dhaka.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We arranged for them to do a video call with their loved ones in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was heartbreaking to see them cry as they spoke to their husbands, fathers, brothers and sons.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was even more heartbreaking that I was meeting many of our cleaners' children even before their fathers even met them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met the daughter, Jannath, of one of our cleaners, Mazibur.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was seven years old and had never met her father before.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I felt bad that Mazibur's daughter met me before meeting her father.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a father, I cannot imagine not being not being there for my daughters' first words, first steps and many other firsts in their lives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am not asking for more for our migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am asking that we be fair to our migrant workers too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2018, I spoke on the Environmental Public Health (Amendment) Bill on the need to ensure that the PWM will apply to cleaners who are hired directly by an F&B establishment and for foreign cleaners.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that we are now ensuring that cleaners who are hired directly by an F&B establishment will get the PWM, but again, what about our migrant cleaners?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2020, I spoke on the Building Control (Amendment) Bill on ensuring that the PWM will apply to our foreign lift technicians as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a matter of fairness, it makes sense for the PWM to apply to all our workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the spirit of increasing productivity and better service standards and quality, it also makes sense for PWM to apply to all our workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Ministry for Sustainability and Environment (MSE) will consider eventually extending the PWM to cover our migrant cleaners and waste disposal workers as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on the conditions under the new cleaning business licensing framework.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The framework will introduce three classes of licences.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can Minister share if the Class 1 licence will also require that no stern warnings or a composition fine was issued against the company?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If not, can Minister share the reasons why not?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, a company acts through the hands and minds of its directors and executive officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There may be cases where prosecutorial direction was exercised not to pursue charges against the company but prosecution was brought against a company’s directors and/or executive officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is public interest in ensuring that the directors and executive officers are personally incentivised to comply with the law.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share if the Ministry will consider also requiring for a Class 1 licence that the directors and executive officers have no conviction history with regard to offences related to the company in the past 24 months?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If not, can the Senior Minister of State share the reasons why not?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My final point is one I am sure Senior Minister of State Amy Khor expects me to raise and so I do not want to disappoint her.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also know that so many Singaporeans are affected by second-hand smoke and they hope the Government will help them and literally save their lives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is not a neighbourly dispute, it is not about being uncomfortable with smelling second-hand smoke and it is not a problem you can adapt to and live with.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is about how second-hand smoke kills and people are trapped and need us to rescue them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad we are doing so much to tackle high-rise littering.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a huge problem on the ground and the amendments in this Bill will help significantly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The introduction of this presumption is recognition of the public interest in catching and deterring high-rise littering given the evidential difficulties and enforcement costs in having to prove who threw the litter out of a flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A problem that poses similar enforcement difficulties and costs is second-hand smoke in flats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second-hand smoke is just as deadly or perhaps even more than high-rise littering and equally needs our urgent attention.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Initially I wondered how NEA could prove the littering, then I found out about the surveillance cameras (though, as I understand it, the main effect is achieved through greater deterrence than the presumption clause).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the key issue was around not being able to prove the culprit was smoking, but if there were surveillance cameras, would this not be possible?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The smoke wafts down, even if we close all our windows and doors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We’ve tried appealing to him (and his landlord).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Both his elder brothers passed away from nose cancer.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is why my husband and I are highly concerned about second-hand smoke." Sir, I hope we can put ourselves in Ms Tham's shoes and imagine her helplessness to protect her family from the silent killer that is second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: One group of changes affects the licensing of cleaning businesses and the roll-out of the Progressive Wage Model for this sector.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Another group of changes relates to the dumping of waste from vehicles and yet another, extends the time period for which an offence can be determined.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, I will raise several points of clarification on areas where there are risks associated with the provisions in this Bill, where I hope the Government can provide some assurances and consider appropriate provisions in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My clarifications and suggestions centre on clause 5 of this amendment Bill which amends section 17 of the original Bill.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: To be clear, littering from residential flats is a serious problem.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It poses public health challenges and lessens quality of life.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: High-rise littering cases are on the increase, as is NEA's deployment of cameras and enforcement actions in respect of high-rise littering.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In spite of the number of cameras and enforcement actions, the level of deterrence embodied in the law and enforcement mechanisms will need stepping up to address the fact that more flats, which are taller and denser, are being built across the island; and the fact that more people are working from home all or some of the time.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It then holds every owner or every tenant of the flat equally liable.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In cases where the offence may have been the result of someone else – say a visitor or workers working in the flat – in such cases, the burden of proof will be on the owner or tenant to prove their innocence in the face of a default assumption of their guilt.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Going forward, when I refer to the owner, I will mean either the owner or tenant depending on what is relevant in each case of an offence.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Must the owner prove this beyond reasonable doubt or can they prove this based on a balance of probabilities?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For example, if there was some other culprit – say a team of workers doing renovation work in the apartment – would the owner need to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that they were not at home at the time of the offence in addition to demonstrating that the works were being done at the time?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Also, can the Government share some examples of what such proof would look like?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Some information from an IT system that shows the location of one's mobile phone and/or computer at the time, for example?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Or the testimony of an eyewitness who is not conflicted, who could place the person somewhere else at that time?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Another scenario – if there are joint owners, would the authorities remove liability from one of the owners if he or she demonstrates that he or she was not present in the flat at the time of the offence, leaving the other owner to bear 100% of the fine?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: One observation I will make here is that if the burden of proof falls on the owner in all cases, this may result in unintended consequences and I will return to that later.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I have another clarification here to put to the Government.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My question is on part (c), what constitutes a reasonable belief?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Is it the legal standard meaning that some evidence must be adduced or merely a belief accompanied by a reason?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Next, HDB flat owners have a greater likelihood of being caught for high-rise littering vis-à-vis private apartment owners.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This is because the new section 17A will only apply to private apartments if the litter lands in "a public place".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This is similar to how the existing prohibition against littering under the Environmental Public Health Act applies only to publicly accessible places, rather than private estates like executive condominiums and strata-titled condominiums.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In Parliament in 2018, the Government said that private estates such as executive condominiums and private strata-titled condominiums are not regarded as such public places in law as access to these places are restricted.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, the management committee of such estates generally have by-laws to deal with high-rise littering and may turn to the courts when dealing with errant residents.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My clarification here is that would the Government work with the Management Corporation Strata Title (MSCT), the committees of private apartment developments to make available its learnings in terms of enforcing these laws and regulations in HDB estates, so that those MCSTs who wish to pursue a more rigorous approach to anti-littering enforcement are able to draw on this experience?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Next, I would like to ask the Government to elaborate on how care will be taken when deciding whether or not to fine or charge vulnerable groups of possible offenders.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: NEA will be sensitive and enforce judiciously against offenders from such groups.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: NEA has in place an existing enforcement framework for the elderly and physically/mentally disabled offenders.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The offender or his/her family members/relatives may write to NEA and provide relevant supporting documents.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In the same vein, owners who may not understand written English and may not be able to read any written notices sent by the NEA may be disadvantaged.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, Sir, I would like to discuss possible unintended consequences arising from this new presumption of guilt embodied in the new clause 17A.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: What if owners require tenants to lock windows as a result of fear of fines?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And what if the new law fuels tension between joint tenants or joint owners who may wish to push the blame to the other?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: To be sure, if these scenarios materialise – I am not saying they necessarily will or to a very great extent – the individuals affected may have other recourse, other means of recourse in law.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: But I raise this point because the new law may, to some degree, have unintended consequences for the dynamics of relationships between and amongst the owners, other residents, tenants and workers living and working in flats.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I hope the Government and other stakeholders will keep an eye on this to be ready to implement changes to the law or to how the law is enforced to address these and other possible unintended consequences.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I recall speaking on the Amendment bill in 2014 and supporting this Bill.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I was hopeful that with the enhanced powers, NEA would be able to reduce the incidences of littering.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Over the past few years, I regularly carried out litter picking exercises in my constituency.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: On each occasion, I get extremely frustrated by the huge amount of litter collected from the public areas.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: You can pick up used face masks, cigarette boxes, plastic bags, drink cans, drink bottles, carton boxes, all of which were thrown onto the ground.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It seems that a small minority of inconsiderate litter bugs have made the environment less pleasant for the majority of residents.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also frequently receive feedback from residents complaining about their upstairs neighbour throwing down lighted cigarettes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Residents are fearful that a lighted cigarette may land inside their flat thereby causing a fire.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They also expressed frustration that NEA could not identify the offender and were unable to stop the high-rise litter.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also get other complaints about residents who throw rice or bread from their flat to feed pigeons.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The pigeons in turn cause a health hazard with the huge amount of pigeon feces all over the ground level.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many Members of Parliament would also have received complaints about high-rise litter bugs who throw food waste, plastic bags, tissue paper and other types of litter – making the ground floor unsafe for residents walking by the area.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I spoke about the issue of littering during Committee of Supply (COS) Debate in 2010 and 2018.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also filed a Parliamentary Question (PQ) in May 2022 asking NEA, what other measures can be taken to prevent littering.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For the same period in 2022, there were around 7,800 cases." In a subsequent Parliamentary reply in October 2022, Minister Grace Fu then said, "feedback on high-rise littering has continued to outpace our efforts to enhance capabilities and measures.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: From 2019 to 2021, the feedback had increased to 22,000, 35,000 and 32,000 cases respectively." The Minister further elaborated that "Investigation into high-rise littering cases remains resource-intensive and time-consuming despite our best efforts.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Effort is required to gather information to guide camera deployments and, subsequently, identify the high-rise littering offender." Sir, this situation is really unacceptable.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: There is a need for the Government to send a strong signal that littering is an anti-social habit that society must frown upon.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When the Keep Singapore Clean campaign was launched on 1 October 1968 by our then-Prime Minister, the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew, the campaign aimed to make Singapore the cleanest and greenest city in the region by addressing the problem of inconsiderate littering.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The campaign sought to instil in Singaporeans the importance of keeping public places clean.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For many years, Singapore was considered one of the cleanest cities in the region.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The onus now falls on the owner or occupier of the flat to identify the person responsible for any litter that originates from the flat.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: First, we should make more use of technology to ensure that litter bugs would be identified.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, in Marine Parade Town Council, we had bought a total number of 73 mini surveillance cameras to be deployed at areas where there are persistent complaints about littering.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: We also installed large signs to tell residents that there are surveillance cameras in the block.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The message to the litter bug is this: if you throw litter from your flat, you will be caught and you have to face the consequences.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The present amendment to the law will assist NEA in that they can then rely on the camera footage and identify the flat from which the litter originates.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It is, thus, for the flat owner or occupier to identify the litter bug staying in the flat.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In addition to any fine imposed, I would like to suggest that NEA impose a Corrective Work Order (CWO) on all littering offenders and they should serve the punishment in the estate where they were caught littering.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In May 2022, I had asked the Minister for Sustainability and Environment about imposing a CWO on littering offenders.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Minister replied then that "we would also like to give first-time offenders a second chance, so that they can learn from their mistakes." I would like to humbly urge the Senior Minister of State to reconsider the position.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: A CWO is meant to assist the littering offender to see for himself the huge amount of litter in the public area and to learn that it is hard work to pick up all the litter in order to keep the estate clean.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And after picking up litter for two hours, the offender should go away with a better understanding that there is an urgent need to keep the public area clean.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If the offender litters again, then double the CWO hours for the second-time offender.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This is a drastic action but for those residents who are not littering offenders, there is really nothing to worry about.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The proposed amendments will also apply to section 17(1)(g) for any ash, hair, feathers, lime, sand, wastepaper or other substances carried by wind in a public place, and also spit or mucus, and that is under section 17A(4).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Is this really desirable, given that the tenants are grown adults and it may not be practicable to expect a landlord to be able to require the obedience of this adult tenant?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: A landlord or tenant who was either not at home or even if he was at home, he might be asleep or working and had no idea whether his tenant or even family members had littered.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And if he had tried asking and no one wanted to own up, would it be fair for an owner to be made responsible or be punished in such circumstances?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Many live-in owners who rent out rooms may be seniors and may not be the best persons to impose themselves on their tenants in this regard.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: What if an owner or live-in landlord, landlady or tenant has reasons to fear an occupier of the flat?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This can be a tenant, a co-tenant or even a family member.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The owner may have cause to be concerned that such a person may become abusive or intimidating.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: What about parents who do not wish to inform on their children?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: What if two unrelated tenants of a public rental flat are confronted with such a complaint?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Unless one owns up readily, one can imagine how such a complaint with the presumption of guilt will cause distress to the household of two.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This new law will put such owners or tenants in a spot vis-à-vis other tenants or family members.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: They may end up taking the blame themselves as passing on the allegation to the other persons may subject him, or her, to some of form of threat or abuse and going to the Police may not always be a desired course of action for a loved one.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If so, will the Senior Minister of State explain how this may work, so that there will be sufficient clarity, as well as certainty?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The prosecution under the new proposed provisions would envisage not just complaints made by a third party who has witnessed litter being thrown down.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: NEA would often have installed cameras after receiving feedback and the cameras would have taken down video footages of littering acts.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I note from the cases I have encountered that NEA may not always install cameras after each complaint.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: High-rise littering is usually committed by a small number of residents.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But their anti‐social and irresponsible acts caused disamenities and unpleasantness to the majority.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Cleaners would have to do additional rounds of cleaning just because of this inconsiderate behaviour.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: They could have done other work for the betterment of residents.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: From my experience, education and anti‐littering messages have no bearing or impact on this minority group, who are the habitual litterers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: They will continue to throw things out of the window because they think they can get away with it.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And indeed, judging by the current means and capabilities that NEA has, there is a high probability that they could throw something out of the window without getting caught.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The passing of this Bill could help raise the deterrent effect but, in my view, it would not be significant enough to deter these habitual litterers that I referred to.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In other words, this new measure is still not the game changer needed.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, I urge NEA to significantly increase capabilities to tackle this high-rise littering problem.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In particular, to harness technologies, as well as to be equipped with forensic means to do the investigations.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: To achieve effective deterrence, NEA would need to beef up its investigative capabilities, step up its zealousness to solve each of the high‐rise littering case.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Often, it takes quite a while for NEA to mobilise its resources to deploy the surveillance equipments.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I believe this is not for lack of trying by the ground NEA officers but, rather, these hardworking officers are just not armed with sufficient tools and ammunition to be effective.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: A case in point is in the Spottiswoode condo killer litter case.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Why would NEA not have the similar capabilities, given the many near fatally high-risk littering posed to the public?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Littered cigarette butts, for example, thrown out of the window, could have caused a fire in the units below them.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In my constituency, I do have many of these long-standing high-rise littering cases which have gone on for years.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: NEA officers has attended to the cases but the littering continues.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Just to pick one case at Blk 203, Petir Road; where residents have raised this for years, but the litterer continues to throw things out of the window.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: If that can be done, it will certainly strengthen the deterrent effect and greatly reduce the incidences of high-rise littering.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These workers are providing essential services and their wages should reflect their valuable contributions.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They should also be adequately compensated for the very challenging nature and conditions of their jobs.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The PWM provides the structure to address these issues and uplift their professions.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The inclusion of these sub-sectors in PWM shows the growing recognition of their very important roles.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is also necessary to have a formal career progression framework to attract more local workers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There are very specific skillsets required to manage effectively and efficiently.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Continuous improvement and retraining are needed to increase productivity in these sectors.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For the new licensing framework, the increase in paid-up capital will provide differentiation among classes of providers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The customers will be able to select suitable companies based on their capabilities and resources.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The system will encourage providers to improve their workflows and innovate to boost productivity and raise service standards.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With greater innovation and increases in productivity, the working conditions of workers in this sector will also improve.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I urge the Ministry to provide more support to these companies to help them and their workers to progress.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, we must also remember that public education, effective usage of recycled materials as well as meaningful partnerships between the industry and Government are equally important components in our anti-littering campaigns and sustainability efforts.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I also hope that Government support can be focused on collaborative partnerships to achieve a zero-waste future for Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, the Ministry can consider allocating Government grants for waste management companies to run public school education campaigns and anti-littering campaigns or channel funding to industry collaborations that encourage the use of recycled materials.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   Public education, effective usage of recycled materials as well as partnerships between the industry and Government play equally important roles in our sustainability efforts.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that Government support can be focused on collaborative partnerships to achieve a zero-waste future for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Waste management and cleaning are essential tasks for the functioning of our society.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are also often physically demanding and hazardous.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must do more to recognise and value the contributions of workers in these sectors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This will make the industry more appealing and safer to work in.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I wish to seek clarifications on three key areas of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, it is imperative that we continue to expand the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) to more groups of workers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I fully endorse diversifying the types of sectors that will benefit from the PWM.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there plans to extend the PWM to other sub-sectors in the industry beyond waste management and materials recovery?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What is the median income of these workers?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, what is the timeline to onboard them onto the PWM?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Likewise, for workers who are not yet on PWM, how will skills upgrading be made more accessible to them?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Before we can even talk about PWM, the workers have to be paid.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As we push for better wages and improved earning power for workers, these efforts come to naught if workers are not paid punctually by their employers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is disheartening to hear of reports where cleaners do not receive their wages on time.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there more recent statistics that indicate whether this situation has improved?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As we seek to enhance the Cleaning Business Licensing Framework, I propose that the track records of companies on timely payment of wages and bonuses should be taken into consideration when they apply for licences.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They should be required to demonstrate that they are proactively resolving this issue before their licences are approved or renewed.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In order for workers to fulfil Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ), I propose that companies should be mandated or incentivised to give workers paid time off from work for training.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Without this, it would firstly be difficult for workers to find the time and energy to attend these courses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, it is only fair that the companies pay for this benefit.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The proposed amendment of "Waste management licensees will be prohibited from deploying individuals in waste management work unless they are employees of waste management licensees" raises questions about who these individuals and workers are.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How many of such workers are there and what percentage of the sector does this represent?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I agree that the proposed amendment is a step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In particular, this will ensure that workers in waste management work are adequately trained and compensated under PWM.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Otherwise, the existing manpower crunch in the sector will only worsen.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, while I support efforts to strengthen the cleaning industry through the Cleaning Business Licensing Framework, it is critical to have specific and viable targets and plans to achieve this.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The framework's goals of developing a skilled and resilient workforce as well as creating better employment opportunities are commendable.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nonetheless, it is important to acknowledge that the demanding nature of the work as well as constant exposure to unsanitary environments has discouraged some individuals from entering the field.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To attract Singaporeans to this sector, we must do more to value the contributions of cleaning and waste management professionals.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This includes enhancing working conditions, incentives and career development opportunities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What are the specific plans and measurable outcomes that have been established to achieve these goals?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What are the tangible incentives for businesses to upgrade from Class 2 to Class 1 licence?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there specific targets for increasing the number of companies making the transition from Class 2 to Class 1 licences?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If so, are the benefits sufficient to incentivise them to do so?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, as we work to strengthen our efforts to combat littering through the implementation of a new statutory presumption clause, it is imperative that we ensure both clarity and robust enforcement.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I fully agree that care and compassion should be exercised in investigating cases involving these groups of people.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, we must also recognise that being elderly or having some form of disability should not be a free pass to commit high-rise littering or any other forms of littering offences.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Flats have rubbish chutes on every floor and some even within their homes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, inconvenience should not be an excuse.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In cases involving children, parents or guardians should bear the responsibility of educating them, especially if it is a repeat offence.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Stronger enforcement measures should be taken if the household continues to be found guilty of littering despite multiple warnings, education attempts or fines.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Unfortunately, there could also be a possibility that disingenuous individuals may push the blame for littering to individuals that are incapable of being found guilty of an offence, such as children under the age of 10.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will investigation officers determine whether these individuals are pushing the blame to children or other mentally incapacitated relatives and tenants in order to escape the penalties?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I understand that there may be operational difficulties in implementing this statutory presumption clause.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I cite as an example a flat owner who leaves his flat for a walk at night when the offence occurred.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How does the owner prove that he was not at home if there is no alibi?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will checks be made against the Police cameras at the lift lobbies?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If the presumption is difficult to rebut, it may be too onerous for residents who have limited abilities or resources to defend themselves.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am also concerned that some flat occupants may act in an inconsiderate manner, thinking that the responsibility is being placed on another tenant or on the owner of the flat.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry share what are the specific targets to determine the effectiveness of this new clause?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What factors will be taken into consideration in measuring its success?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What other plans and measures is the Government considering to bring down the number of high-rise littering cases?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nevertheless, to truly tackle this problem, we cannot just rely on one or two tweaks.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We need a systematic and comprehensive approach that addresses the underlying causes of littering and focus on how to tackle the issue effectively.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We need to move beyond industry development and enforcement.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: One key lever is through education and changing norms and behaviour.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must embrace a culture that reduces waste, avoids buying unnecessary items and practises consumption in moderation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: By doing so, we create less waste and have less of a need to manage it.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Besides, we must all strive to adopt and maintain good social habits to keep our environment and community clean.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: No number of cleaners or cleaning technology can keep up with the daily littering habits of hundreds and thousands of residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, deploying more cleaners ultimately leads to higher service and conservancy (S&CC) fees.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This may perpetuate the mentality that residents are paying for the service and should make the most use of it.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I recognise that public education on these issues is challenging and takes time.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But public education is still essential for creating a society that is civic-minded, considerate and cares for the environment.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must persist in our efforts and work towards fostering a culture of sustainability and environmental responsibility.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is critical to preserve our environment and ensure a sustainable future for generations to come.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: More and more new buildings will be equipped with pneumatic waste conveying systems.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Undoubtedly, besides increased productivity, such systems also bring other benefits, such as environmental benefits and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   I support the new regulations on high-rise littering from HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is reasonable to assume that the registered landlord or tenant is the offender.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If the person who litters is a guest of an HDB unit, the owner is also responsible for taking care of this problem.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For some, fines and Corrective Work Orders (CWOs) are not enough to curb this bad habit of high-rise littering.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This should greatly reduce the chances of random throwing, especially for those with mental or psychological problems, including those with dementia and those with special needs.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For now, camera footage can only occasionally capture those throwing litter from the windows.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In order to avoid being accused of violating personal privacy, the cameras can only be aimed at the outer walls.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A resident asked me if residents living below the offending units could be allowed to install cameras pointing upwards from their windows in an attempt to identify residents throwing rubbish from above, while not violating their privacy.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These large quantities of waste can cause safety and environmental issues, especially in newly completed HDB blocks where they accumulate in large quantities.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this case, it should not be hard to figure out the identity of those culprits.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope the Minister will consider the above suggestions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Speaker, Sir, Singapore has very strict laws to maintain law and order and littering of any kind is an offence.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: However, even with such strict laws, we will still require an army of more than 40,000 resident cleaners and 3,000 waste collection crew to ensure Singapore remains a clean and green city.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This Bill proposing to implement the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) for workers in the waste collection and materials recovery sub-sectors is one that I support wholeheartedly.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Waste collection is tough, physically demanding work and gruelling.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Rain or shine, these workers will be out there collecting our trash.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This is difficult work and such jobs will not appeal to most Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: At present, there are about 3,000 resident waste collectors.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Many of them have young families with school-going children to support.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In order to assist them, we should provide opportunities for them to learn new job skills and be able to earn a higher salary.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The pandemic has effectively raised the gross monthly salaries of waste collection workers in the major waste companies to above $3,000.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Currently, there are three main public waste collectors, namely SembWaste, 800 Super and Alba W&H Smart City that are appointed by NEA to collect waste from domestic and trade premises across the entire country.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: During the period when there were border shutdowns, it was difficult to hire foreigners to assist us in this sector.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Thus, the major waste collection companies had to increase wages in order to attract locals so that the companies can fulfil their contractual service level requirements.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: And the response was acceptable as the wage increases proved to be quite effective!

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Although the bigger players in the industry have largely moved ahead with wage increases, PWM will formalise the salary increase across the entire industry.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Smaller waste collection companies will also need to keep up with the revised pay structure accordingly.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The PWM for the waste collection industry will ensure fair remuneration to these essential workers for their indispensable services.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We hope this wage model will be able to attract certain younger workers to have an open mind and join the sector and assist us to maintain our public hygiene and health standards.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Needless to say, it will be extremely challenging to attract younger people to work in this sector and deploying more valuable manpower resources just to collect waste will be a daunting task.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We will have to leverage on technology, better design and changes in work processes.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In recent years, the waste industry has undertaken commendable efforts to automate the waste collection process.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: For instance, the most commonly seen Rear-End-Loading (REL) waste trucks are operated by three staff – a driver and two attendants.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: With the push of a button, the loader will tip the waste containers over and dump the waste into the truck.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This helps the attendants with the heavy lifting.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: However, this is only possible after some necessary adjustments are made.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The REL trucks will need to be automated more.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Since April 2018, the new huge blue recycling bins have gradually replaced their older and smaller predecessors in many towns.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The new blue recycling bin is a good example of how technology and design can help to save manpower.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Hence, a typical three-men team can now be reduced to only the driver who doubles up as the operator.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: However, there are still constraints on the ground which pose limitations to proliferating these large blue bins across all parts of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: For instance, in private estates with narrow driveways, the side-loader trucks do not have sufficient clearance to position itself precisely for the automated loading of the recycling bins.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Hence, an attendant may still be required to complete this last mile.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
